chapter_mission: Open the Ankhural Codex fragment. Deliver the lattice-as-imposed-structure framework experientially, not didactically. Expose Torin's rationalization as intellectually seductive. Hit the ship alarm — the next Corridor stop has been breached ahead of them.
chapter_turn: Ben catches himself agreeing with Torin's reading of the Codex before he pulls back. The threat is not that the technique's defenders are obviously wrong; it is that they are elegant, and he is susceptible. Sera, in a private corridor, names the argument for what it is: she heard it from Gavran.

scene_plan.purpose: Common area. Sera breaks the seal on the Codex case. Every Force-sensitive in the room feels the artifact's resonance before anyone speaks. Ben touches it and the experiential flash lands: the Force present, unstructured, no direction, no moral feedback — a handful of seconds and his hand jerks back. R06 delivered by sensation, not paragraph. Four different Force presences react four different ways around the table.

Torin lifts the Codex without flinching. He holds it steady while everyone else watches for a reaction that does not come. His rationalization crystallises — if the lattice is imposed, the technique is not violation but correction. He is persuasive enough that Ben catches his own head nodding before he stops it. In the corridor afterward, Sera's hand on Ben's arm, back to the door: 'I have heard that argument before. From a man I followed into a war.'

Ship alarm. Desh in the cockpit in three seconds. The Brotherhood Outpost — the next Corridor stop — has been breached. Energy spikes days old, not active. They are not walking into an ambush; they are walking into a scene Veraine left for them. Approach. Moderate thin place with dark-side residue bleeding through the lattice's holes. H09 advances.

relationship_turns.from: private alliance — corridor warning about Torin (Ch8)
relationship_turns.to: shared pattern-recognition — Sera trusts Ben enough to name Gavran in the same sentence as Torin. The analogy is now between them, not in her head
active susceptibility — Ben has felt Torin's argument as correct for two seconds before catching it. Torin does not yet know this. Ben will not forget it
quietly validated — the Codex's framework reads as evidence for his 'whose cage has nicer bars' position, but the evidence is not triumph; it is one more argument he has not been asked for

exit_vector: Approach to the Brotherhood Outpost. The Force ahead leaking dark-side residue through gaps in the lattice — oil through cracked pavement. Desh on the controls; Ben braced at the doorframe. Torin leaning toward it without realising he is. The caravan is now a chase, and the chase is not a chase.
notes: R06 is the intellectual heart of the novel and the highest didactic-risk delivery. It must be received as sensation, not explained as thesis. Ben's flash of unstructured Force in s1 is the reader's first taste of the full de-structuring that lands at Ch13 — mild preview, auditory/somatic vocabulary only, no analytical paragraph. Use force_mechanics.vocabulary_variation — lean on somatic or acoustic families here, not the structural/handrail family from earlier chapters. Torin's rationalization in s2 must be genuinely compelling on the page; if the reader thinks Torin is obviously wrong, the book loses him. Voice: Zahn-compact in the opening beat, debate precision in s2, procedural urgency in s3. Anti-patterns: (a) no one quotes the Codex verbatim at length — we receive it through reaction; (b) Sera's warning is a single line and a hand on an arm, not a monologue; (c) the alarm in s3 must land before the Codex debate reaches a conclusion — no tidy resolution.
